bull_bear.body:
- Over the last 5 decades the Company has earned the status of being the most preferred supplier of steel for critical applications
- Strategic alliance with Mukand Limited at the Ginigera integrated facility, with production sharing and cost sharing through the Hospet Steels Limited joint venture
- Stated strategic priority of backward integration to strengthen control over raw material quality, and of forward-integrated value-added facilities
- Breadth of end-user exposure across commercial vehicles, passenger vehicles, two wheelers, diesel engines, bearings, tractors, wind turbines, oil and gas and railways
- Association with the Kalyani group - the Chairman is Chairman and Managing Director of Bharat Forge Limited, a key customer industry participant
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Air emissions and air quality management — Identified in the BRSR as a material risk with negative financial implication because production is derived from the MBF route, which is an emission-intensive process; mitigation is a commitment to prevent, abate and mitigate air emissions and to adopt best available technologies.
- Health and safety — Flagged as a material risk - non-compliance with safety measures may lead to liabilities and operational and financial loss, and incidents may adversely affect employee morale and Company reputation; mitigated through health care services at each location and regular training.
- Water availability and consumption — The Company requires a large quantity of water in its processes; water is a vital yet limited resource and its scarcity poses a significant risk with negative impact. Mitigation is optimum consumption through Reduce, Recycle and Reuse and a Wastewater Treatment Plant treating 100% of wastewater into reusable water.
- Human capital - attracting, developing and retaining talent — Listed as a material risk in the BRSR; mitigation is employee-friendly policies and practices for growth, development and work satisfaction. The permanent-employee turnover disclosure in the same report shows meaningful attrition across FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26.
- Concentration on a single manufacturing activity and on the domestic forging / automotive value chain — Structural rather than labelled: manufacturing of forging and engineering quality carbon and alloy steel, pig iron and foundry coke accounts for 97.03% of turnover, and exports contribute only 0.59% of total turnover, so the business is almost entirely exposed to Indian forging and vehicle-component demand.
- Dependence on demand dynamics in domestic and export markets (economic performance) — Framed in the BRSR as an opportunity - identification of evolving demand dynamics helps in meeting operational guidance - with the response being introduction of value-added products and product diversification per customer requirements; the flip side is exposure to demand cycles.
- Foreign exchange exposure — The Directors' Report states foreign exchange risk is managed with appropriate hedging activities using Forward Exchange Contracts against firm commitments, and that there were no materially uncovered exchange risks.
- Customer satisfaction and retention — Treated in the BRSR as an opportunity with positive financial outcomes, addressed through increased customer interaction on quality requirements, quicker response times and long-term agreements with customers - implying dependence on sustaining those long-term customer relationships.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures forging and engineering quality carbon and alloy steel, pig iron and foundry coke, an activity that accounted for 97.03% of its turnover in FY 2025-26. Its products - rolled products, as cast blooms and rounds, pig iron and foundry coke - are sold primarily to the Indian forging industry, with Indian and international component manufacturers forming a significant part of the clientele. Manufacturing is carried out at the integrated steel facility at Ginigera, which operates under a strategic alliance with Mukand Limited and is managed and operated by the joint venture Hospet Steels Limited.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Deepen the portfolio of value-added and specialised steel solutions for India's most critical sectors - infrastructure, mobility, defence, renewable energy, aerospace, nuclear power and advanced manufacturing - strengthening self-reliance in materials the nation can no longer afford to import
- Continue investing in technology, operational excellence, talent development and sustainable manufacturing practices to remain future-ready and participate in emerging opportunities from next-generation sectors such as electric mobility, aerospace and defence
- Invest in advanced manufacturing, process automation and digitalization to raise quality, sharpen efficiency and improve responsiveness to customers
- Work with customers through metallurgical and product development teams to engineer steels meeting the most exacting performance standards; quality treated as a discipline running through every process rather than a department
- Sustain profitability in a year of top-line pressure through cost management discipline, focused execution and operational excellence
- Lower the environmental footprint of steelmaking, including through long-term renewable energy procurement
- Build a safety culture in which every individual returns home unharmed, and nurture a future-ready workforce through continuous learning and capability building
- Retain the position of preferred supplier of alloy steel products for global customers, guided by over five decades of metallurgical expertise and enduring customer partnerships
- The routed sections state policy intent rather than payout figures. Declaration of dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 is placed as ordinary business at the Fifty-Third Annual General Meeting. The Company has not accepted any deposit under Chapter V of the Companies Act, 2013 during the year. Related party dealings are governed by a Board-approved Related Party Transactions Policy, with all such transactions on arm's length basis and in the ordinary course of business, reviewed and pre-approved by the Audit Committee and noted quarterly; material related party transactions with Bharat Forge Limited and Kalyani Technoforge Limited for FY 2027-28 are placed before members for approval. CSR spending is directed at education in the locations in which the Company operates. Risk management is embedded in strategy setting and decision making through a Risk Management Committee, with the Audit Committee holding additional oversight of financial risks and controls.
- Certifications adopted and mapped to the NGRBC principles: ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management for manufacturing of plain carbon and alloy steel rolled products), IATF 16949 First Edition (Automotive Quality Management System), ISO 14001:2015 (Environment Management System), ISO 45001:2018 (Health & Safety Management System) and the IBR Well-known Steel Maker Certificate from the Central Boilers Board
- Operates a Wastewater Treatment Plant that treats 100% of the wastewater into reusable water, with optimum water consumption ensured through the 3 R's - Reduce, Recycle and Reuse
- Commitment to preventing, abating and mitigating emissions to air, adopting best available technologies to reduce air emissions from the emission-intensive MBF route
- Director's statement: committed to integrating Environmental, Social and Governance principles into the business, and to reducing environmental impact by continuously exploring ways to improve operational efficiency, reduce fossil fuel consumption and increase usage of greener materials
- All nine NGRBC principles are covered by Board-approved policies translated into procedures, but the policies do not extend to value chain partners (answered 'N' for all nine principles)
- The BRSR reports 'N.A.' against specific commitments, goals and targets with defined timelines, and against performance versus such targets - i.e. no time-bound ESG targets are disclosed
- Highest authority responsible for implementation and oversight of the Business Responsibility policies is the Managing Director; the Company does not have a specified Board committee or director responsible for decision making on sustainability related issues
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for communities, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, with web links to the policy; no complaints are reported as pending at the close of the year
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no named capex project, commissioning date or capacity-addition timeline. Expansion appears only as a stated strategic priority: under 'Leadership in Alloy Steel Industry' the Company intends to increase capacity through brownfield and greenfield expansions or strategic acquisitions, aligned with market demand and long-term goals, while attaining cost leadership by improving operational efficiency and optimising resource utilisation. Under 'Backward & Forward Integration' it intends to strengthen control over raw material quality through backward integration and to proactively evaluate evolving customer needs and invest in forward-integrated, value-added facilities. The Chairman's message frames the opportunity set - electric mobility, aerospace and defence - that this future capability build is meant to serve, but attaches no project, capacity number or date to it.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- As India moves up the manufacturing value chain, the demand for high-quality specialty steel will continue to expand
- India's crude steel production crossed 168 Million tons during FY 2026 versus about 151 Million tons in FY 2025, growth of over 11%, reinforcing India's position as the world's second-largest steel producer
- India's finished steel consumption increased to approximately 164 Million tons, driven by robust demand from infrastructure, construction, railways, automotive, engineering and capital goods sectors
- Global crude steel production declined by nearly 2% during CY 2025 as demand remained weak across several regions; China's real estate slowdown drove higher Chinese exports and increased pressure on international steel prices
- Geopolitical conflicts, protectionist trade measures and trade restrictions created additional uncertainty across supply chains and commodity markets
- Automotive demand - a major contributor to the Company's portfolio - crossed pre-pandemic levels across all vehicle types in FY 2026: PV at an all-time high of 5.5 Million vehicles (about 9% growth), CV at 1.2 Million (13% growth), 2W at 26.8 Million (13% growth) and 3W at 1.3 Million
- Increasing customer focus on supply chain resilience and self-reliance - customers seeking reliable domestic suppliers with consistent quality, technical support and specialized products - is particularly favourable for value-added and specialty steel manufacturers such as Kalyani Steels
- Government investments in roads, railways, defence, energy and urban infrastructure continue to create significant opportunities for domestic steel producers
- India remained the fastest-growing major economy with GDP growth of 7.7% in FY 2026 versus 7.1% in FY 2025, driven by strong domestic demand, infrastructure push and manufacturing expansion
- The Company is running close to 100% capacity utilization, so near-term volume is constrained by available capacity
